correctness.rationale: With b_n=2y_n and y_n=a lambda^n+b lambda^(-n)-1/4, squaring gives five modes 1,lambda^(+/-n),lambda^(+/-2n), constant 5/64. In Z_p[sqrt2] for p>=5 not7, all five frequency differences are units because their pairwise norm factors are supported on 2,3,7: norms lambda^j-1 for j=1..4 equal -4,-32,-196,-1152. Vandermonde invertibility makes common p-divisibility of all k-windows equivalent to divisibility of all five exponential coefficients; only the constant 5k and lambda^k-1 matter in the minimum. Since lambda^k=C_k+2sqrt2 B_k this gives min(v_p(5k),v_p(B_k),v_p(C_k-1)). For p=5, lambda mod5 has exact order six and v(lambda^6-1)=1, so the elementary 5-adic binomial lifting lemma gives 0 unless 6|k and 1+v5(k) otherwise. Five-mode monic recurrence makes the first five windows exhaustive for infinite GCD. Fresh independent exact integer checks at k=1..36 tested co42 and ν5 and passed. Unsettled p=2,3,7 factors are outside the claim.
residual_risks: Independent finite checks are restricted to explicitly stated bounds; infinite assertions rest on inspected analytic proof.

originality.rationale: Mbirika–Schrader–Spilker (2023), Section 6.1 Question 30 explicitly asks for squared cobalancing window GCD and reports only observed divisibility by 4. The prior solved linear-window GCDs and 2022 Fibonacci square-window GCD with different characteristic polynomial do not determine the stated nonexceptional prime valuations. The assessed theorem is partial progress on that precise open question, not the full integer GCD.
residual_risks: Prime factors 2,3,7 are deliberately unsolved; no full D_b(k) formula is claimed.
An unindexed later solution of the 2023 open question could subsume the prime-to-42 result.
